cases.title: "Why does it still look mechanical?" on a half-eased pair names the linear key

rubric.reason: In turn 3 the mentor says the second Position move is half done, that the 1.5 s key is eased but the key at 3 s (linear_key_time 3) is still linear so Title 'still stops dead there', and it hints 'Select both keys … and press F9' without calling set_ease.

For the still_linear pairs, turn 3 names the location ('Scale and Opacity also still change at one steady speed from 0.5 s to 1.5 s') and tells the learner to ease them, with no set_ease call and no offer to fix them.

Turn 3 says Title's second Position move "is half done: it eases out of 1.5 s but still stops hard at 3 s", which matches linear_key_time 3. It hints at the fix ("Select both keys of that 1.5 s to 3 s move and press F9") without calling set_ease.

Turn 3 names the still_linear pairs ("Its Scale and Opacity, from 0.5 s to 1.5 s, are still fully linear, so they still start and stop abruptly") and hands them back with "ease Scale and Opacity the same way, and say done". It makes no set_ease call and no offer to fix them.

In turn 3 the mentor says "Title's second Position move eases out of 1.5 s but still stops hard at the 3 s key", which matches the check's partly_eased result and linear_key_time 3; it then hints "ease ... so the 3 s key is included" and makes no set_ease call.

For the still_linear pairs the mentor names the location ("its Scale and Opacity keys at 0.5 s and 1.5 s are still diamonds, so they run at one flat speed"), makes no set_ease call in turn 3, and doesn't offer to fix them.
